Classic Fuzztones for the Modern age The SGFX Fuzzbox is a modern evolution of one of the most iconic fuzz circuits ever made, the Tone Bender Mk II. Originally developed in mid-’60s England, the Mk II helped define the sound of British rock with its thick, harmonically rich tone and incredible response to a player’s touch. It became an extension of the guitar itself, cleaning up with the volume knob and exploding into rich, singing sustain when pushed. That unmistakable sound found its way onto countless recordings and stages in the hands of players like Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Mick Ronson. These artists helped shape fuzz into something expressive, dynamic, and unmistakably musical. Fuzzbox builds on that legacy with a refined silicon design that preserves the character and responsiveness of the original while expanding its range and control. The goal isn’t to recreate one particular vintage unit, but to capture the essence of what made the Mk II so inspiring and give you the tools to shape it around your own sound and playing style. BUILT AROUND FEEL Fuzzbox was designed around the idea that great fuzz is about feel as much as sound. Rather than chasing an exact clone of a single vintage unit, we focused on capturing the response, harmonic richness, and dynamic interaction that made the original Mk II circuits so inspiring in the first place. Carefully selected low-gain silicon transistors deliver the warmth, aggression, and touch sensitivity of classic British fuzz, while expanded control over voltage and bias allows the pedal to move far beyond the limitations of traditional vintage designs. The result is a fuzz that feels alive under your hands—raw and expressive, yet refined enough for modern rigs and real-world use. MODERN/VINTAGE INPUT TOGGLE The Fuzzbox features a two-position Vintage/Modern toggle that dramatically changes the feel and response of the pedal. Vintage mode delivers the raw, immediate character of a classic Mk II-style fuzz, with direct interaction between your guitar and the circuit for dynamic cleanup and explosive attack. Flip to Modern mode and the input response becomes smoother and more controlled, with added low-end presence and improved compatibility with wah pedals, buffers, and larger pedalboard setups. Same core fuzz voice—two distinct ways to hit it. VOLTAGE SAG & BIAS CONTROLS The addition of dedicated Bias and Sag controls gives Fuzzbox a wide range of feel and response beyond traditional vintage fuzz circuits. Bias adjusts the operating point of the third transistor, allowing you to fine-tune the texture and character of the fuzz from tighter and focused to softer and more compressed. The Sag control acts like a variable, fading battery—reducing the overall circuit voltage from a firm, punchy response to a smoother, more yielding attack with natural compression. SolidGoldFX browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive fuzz browse by enclosure pedal SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox - Vintage/Modern Fuzz Published on September 20, 2026 SolidGoldFX fuzz pedal Information The SolidGoldFX Fuzzbox is a modern take on the Tone Bender Mk II, the circuit developed in mid-1960s England that went on to define the sound of British rock. That original was thick and harmonically rich, and responsive enough to a player's touch that it worked as an extension of the guitar rather than simply a distortion, cleaning up as the volume knob rolled back and opening into singing sustain when pushed. It reached records and stages through players including Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Mick Ronson. Rather than copying one particular vintage unit, the Fuzzbox rebuilds the idea around carefully selected low-gain silicon transistors, which hold onto the warmth and harmonic texture of the original design while behaving consistently from one pedal to the next. On top of that it exposes the two variables that most define how a fuzz reacts but are usually fixed inside the box: the bias of the circuit and the voltage feeding it. Bias adjusts the operating point of the third transistor, which has a large effect on both voice and feel. Wound down it produces a gated, splatty texture with more aggression; wound up it smooths out into a fuller sound with more conventional sustain. Sag simulates a dying battery across a range of roughly 9 V down to 5 V. Fully counterclockwise, at full voltage, the pedal stays tight, punchy, and stable; as it advances and the voltage drops, the attack softens, compression builds, and the circuit falls into the starved behavior associated with old fuzz tones. Between them the pedal covers tight and articulate through to sputtering and collapsing without falling apart musically. Alongside those, Level sets output and Fuzz sets the amount of saturation, opening from a gritty, more open drive at lower settings into thick, compressed, sustaining fuzz further up. In practice the two interact. Sag and Bias both wound up gives a buzzsaw texture with a torn, Velcro-like edge; backing Sag off reduces the starved-battery behavior and returns sustain. Born in mid-sixties England, the original design helped shape the raw, high-gain landscape of early rock in the hands of legends like Jimmy Page, Jeff Beck, and Mick Ronson. It wasn’t merely distortion; it functioned as a living extension of the guitar, cleaning up organically with a roll of the volume knob and blooming into singing, harmonic sustain when pushed. Instead of chasing an unyielding, museum-piece clone, the Fuzzbox focuses entirely on feel. At its heart are carefully selected low-gain silicon transistors engineered to deliver the warmth, bite, and touch sensitivity of vintage gear, but with the reliability and range required for contemporary setups. The pedal relies heavily on tactile control to bridge vintage grit with modern utility: Vintage/Modern Toggle: The Vintage setting provides the raw, immediate response of a classic Mk II, maximizing direct guitar-to-circuit interaction for explosive attack. Flipping to Modern smooths out the input, introduces a fuller low-end presence, and ensures seamless compatibility with buffers, wah pedals, and crowded boards. Bias Control: Adjusts the operating point of the third transistor, shifting the texture from a tight, focused grind to a softer, more saturated crunch. Sag Control: Mimics the behavior of a fading battery by scaling internal voltage down from 9V to 5V, yielding a yielding, naturally compressed attack. The result is a deeply expressive, highly responsive stompbox that honors classic British fire while giving players total command over their tone.
